sub_answers.text: Several companies developed merchandising and media tie-ins for the series, including a trading card game and video games [d360759s0p0]. sub_answers.text: A live-action TV adaptation of Vicky the Viking was announced in February 2018 by Studio 100/Studio 100 Media and m4e in partnership with German Rat Pack Filmproduktion, with Ulli Stoef and Christian Becker named as co-producers [d1642030s4p0]. One Piece was adapted into an anime by Toei Animation (premiered October 1999), had a festival film by Production I.G, fourteen animated feature films and an OVA developed by Toei, and a Netflix live-action TV series released in 2023; English-language licensing was handled by Viz Media (North America/UK) and Madman Entertainment (Australia) [d360759s0p0]. Lucky Star’s anime was produced by Kyoto Animation and aired April 8–September 16, 2007, with a director change from Yutaka Yamamoto to Yasuhiro Takemoto; Kadokawa Pictures USA and Bandai Entertainment licensed the series for English release (Bandai released multiple DVD volumes and a boxed set) and Funimation later re-licensed and released it on Blu-ray/DVD July 12, 2016 [d4778915s3p0]. Pani Poni Dash! was licensed in North America by Funimation and in the United Kingdom by ADV Films, with King Records’ Starchild holding video and music rights; a special OVA was released April 15, 2009 and Funimation released a complete DVD box March 10, 2009 (and re-released it October 26, 2010) [d8158955s0p0]. Bleach spawned four theatrical films directed by Noriyuki Abe, had Warner Bros. in talks for a live-action adaptation (producers Peter Segal and Michael Ewing were attached, later Dan Mazeau as screenwriter and Masi Oka as producer), and a Japanese live-action film directed by Shinsuke Sato starring Sota Fukushi was released July 20, 2018; Aniplex released related drama CDs [d1397721s8p0].
